_meta.name: The Casefile
_meta.note: Investigations, not single decisions. Each case gives a limited budget of analyst hours; actions spend them and return evidence. The decisive evidence is deliberately not reachable by doing everything — you must choose. 'truth' is what was actually happening; 'epilogue' is what the institution finds out later.

schema.actions[].reveals: evidence key returned; null means the line goes nowhere
schema.decisive: evidence keys required to reach the right call on the merits

cases.title: Six deposits, one grieving customer
cases.subject: Ms L. Peeters · retail · customer since 2011
cases.brief: Cash deposits totalling €53,400 over eleven days on an account that has never seen cash. The rule fired on threshold proximity.
cases.opening: Fourteen years of salary in, card spend out. Then six deposits between €8,000 and €9,600, all under the reporting threshold, across two branches. The pattern is textbook structuring. Textbook patterns have textbook explanations too.

actions.name: Pull 24-month transaction history
actions.hint: Establish what normal looks like before deciding what abnormal means.

actions.name: Ask the customer for source of funds

e_tx.title: 24 months of history
e_tx.body: Salary of €3,180 monthly, card spend, one standing order. No cash activity of any size until 2 March. The six deposits are the only cash events in the entire period.

e_kyc.title: KYC file
e_kyc.body: Identity verified 2011 with Belgian ID, refreshed 2019. Occupation: nurse, university hospital. No corporate interests. Risk rating: low. Nothing has changed on the file.

e_rm.title: Relationship manager
e_rm.body: "She came in personally each time. Said she'd rather not carry it around. Her mother passed in January — I remember because she mentioned the funeral."

e_source.title: Source of funds — customer response
e_source.body: Customer provides a notarial succession deed dated 14 February. Estate included €54,000 held in cash in a safe deposit box, itemised in the inventory. Deposits total €53,400. She apologises for splitting them and says the branch advised her not to carry more than €10,000 at once.

e_media.title: Adverse media
e_media.body: No results. One namesake in a Dutch local newspaper, different age and city, unrelated.

e_peer.title: Peer group comparison
e_peer.body: Cash deposit behaviour is unusual for the salaried-professional segment, but the segment is broad and the comparison adds nothing the history has not already shown.

close.title: Closed, with the source documented
close.body: The notarial deed makes the pattern explicable and the file defensible. Note what made this closeable: not the absence of a red flag — the flag was real and correctly raised — but a verified, documented explanation that reconciles with the amounts.

rfi.title: Sent back for information you could have obtained
rfi.body: Reasonable, but you had the authority to ask directly. The RFI route adds a week and lands on someone else's desk.

escalate.title: Escalated a documented inheritance
escalate.body: Investigations will spend two days reaching the answer a single phone call would have produced. This is how queues stop working: not through laziness but through unwillingness to close.

sar.title: Reported an inheritance as suspicious
sar.body: A report with no articulable suspicion behind it. Defensive filing degrades the intelligence the FIU receives, and it happened to a bereaved customer whose account may now be exited.

cases.epilogue_wrong: Three months later the customer moves her account. The complaint file notes she provided a notarial deed on request and was never told the outcome.
cases.law: AMLR Art. 69 — structuring is reportable; Art. 20 — CDD proportionate to risk. A pattern that matches a typology is a reason to ask, not a conclusion.
cases.lesson: Structuring detection is trivially easy to write and produces enormous noise. The skill is not spotting the pattern — the system did that. It is knowing which single question resolves it, and asking that one first.

cases.title: Machinery that never leaves the port
cases.subject: Meridian Trading BVBA · corporate · high risk · customer since 2019
cases.brief: Four payments totalling €620,000 to a UAE intermediary for parts shipped directly from Pakistan. Invoice values look high.
cases.opening: The customer imports industrial parts and has done for six years. The payments are routine in shape. What is not routine is the intermediary that appeared four months ago, and the fact that the goods never touch the country billing for them.

actions.name: Establish beneficial ownership of the intermediary

e_tx.title: Payment history
e_tx.body: Six years of payments to eleven suppliers across Türkiye, Italy and Germany. Gulf Machinery FZE appears for the first time in December, and now accounts for 71% of outbound value.

e_invoice.title: The four invoices
e_invoice.body: Hydraulic control units, quantities 40–60 per shipment, unit prices between €3,100 and €3,900. Invoices are well formed. Terms: payment on issue, no retention.

e_price.title: Market price benchmark
e_price.body: Comparable hydraulic control units from three EU distributors: €1,850–€2,240. The invoiced prices sit 58–74% above the top of that range, consistently, across all four shipments. On €620,000 of payments, roughly €250,000 has no goods behind it.

e_ubo.title: Beneficial ownership of Gulf Machinery FZE
e_ubo.body: Incorporated four months ago. Sole corporate shareholder registered in a jurisdiction with no public register; nominee director provided by a corporate services firm. Beneficial owner cannot be established. One address match with a company previously owned by Meridian's own director.

e_ship.title: Shipping documentation
e_ship.body: Bills of lading show Karachi to Antwerp, direct. The UAE appears nowhere in the transport chain. The intermediary handles no goods.

e_media.title: Adverse media
e_media.body: Nothing on Meridian. Nothing on Gulf Machinery FZE — it is four months old and has no footprint at all, which is itself unremarkable for a new entity.

e_rm.title: Relationship manager
e_rm.body: "Good client, always pays, never a problem. They mentioned restructuring their supply chain for tax reasons. I didn't ask further."

e_credit.title: Credit file
e_credit.body: Facilities performing. No arrears. Turnover consistent with declared activity.

close.title: Closed a value-transfer scheme
close.body: Roughly €250,000 of unsupported value moved out through invoices you accepted at face value. The intermediary was a conduit and the pricing was the proof.

rfi.title: Asked the customer to explain their own scheme
rfi.body: You have gone back to the party operating the structure and invited them to justify it. They will, plausibly, and the file will now contain their explanation as though it were evidence.

escalate.title: Escalated to investigations
escalate.body: Defensible, and investigations will get there. But you had the two facts that make the case — pricing and ownership — and escalation without articulating them just moves the work.

sar.title: Reported, with the value gap articulated
sar.body: The report names what makes this suspicious: an intermediary handling no goods, systematic over-invoicing quantified against market, and a beneficial owner that cannot be established. That is a report an FIU analyst can act on.

cases.epilogue_wrong: Eleven months later the FIU requests records for Meridian in connection with a sanctions-evasion network. The bank's file shows the alert was raised and dismissed without the pricing ever being checked.
cases.law: AMLR Art. 34 — EDD where a transaction has no apparent economic purpose; Art. 22 — beneficial ownership of counterparties; Art. 69 — reporting.
cases.lesson: Trade-based laundering hides inside legitimate commerce, which is why it is the most used and least detected typology. It is not visible in the transaction — it is visible in the price. Almost no bank benchmarks pricing, and that is precisely the gap being used.

cases.title: Eleven accounts that behave like one
cases.subject: Retail cohort · payments institution · onboarded within 60 days
cases.brief: A single account flagged for pass-through activity. It does not look like much on its own.
cases.opening: One account: money in from strangers, money out within hours, balance returning to zero. Handled alone it is a small case. The question is whether it is alone.

actions.name: Look for accounts with the same behavioural signature
Check device and IP overlap across accounts
Adverse media on the account holder

e_tx.title: Flagged account
e_tx.body: €47,200 in from twelve unrelated private senders over nine days, €46,850 out to three accounts in Poland, Lithuania and Romania. Holder is 21, declared a student job at onboarding.

e_cohort.title: Behavioural cohort
e_cohort.body: Eleven accounts share the signature: onboarded within a 60-day window, dormant 2–3 weeks, then pass-through activity of €40k–€60k each. Aggregate €512,000. Nine of the eleven send onward to the same three destination accounts.

e_device.title: Device and IP overlap
e_device.body: Seven of the eleven accounts were opened from the same device fingerprint. Four share an IP block used during onboarding but never afterwards. The account holders do not appear to know each other.

e_onboard.title: Onboarding records
e_onboard.body: All eleven passed identity verification with genuine documents. The identities are real. The holders are real. Nothing in onboarding failed.

e_victim.title: Fraud cross-reference
e_victim.body: Nineteen of the inbound senders across the cohort appear in fraud complaints — investment scams and marketplace fraud. Funds are victim proceeds.

e_ask.title: Contact the account holder
e_ask.body: No response to two attempts. Note: contacting a suspected mule risks tipping off the network operating the accounts, and the transaction record already establishes the pattern.

e_media.title: Adverse media
e_media.body: Nothing. Twenty-one-year-old with no public footprint.

close.title: Closed one account and left ten running
close.body: The single account was small. The network was not. Victim funds continued to move through the other ten for as long as they stayed open.

rfi.title: Contacted a suspected mule
rfi.body: Beyond the delay, this risks tipping off the network operating the accounts — and the answer would not have changed what the transaction data already showed.

escalate.title: Escalated the single account
escalate.body: Correct instinct on the account in front of you. But if you escalated without the cohort, investigations receive one small case rather than a network, and the other ten stay open.

sar.title: Reported the network
sar.body: Eleven linked accounts, a shared device fingerprint, common destinations and identified victim funds. This is a report that lets an FIU see a structure rather than an incident.

cases.epilogue_wrong: Four months later, three of the remaining accounts appear in a police request. Total victim losses routed through the institution during the intervening period: €338,000.
cases.law: AMLR Art. 25 — ongoing monitoring; Art. 69 — reporting. TFR where onward transfers lack originator data.
cases.lesson: Mule networks are invisible one account at a time and obvious in aggregate. The decisive move is not deeper analysis of the flagged account — it is asking whether anything else behaves the same way. Most alert queues are structured to prevent exactly that question.

cases.title: A shareholder just under the line
cases.subject: Northwind Logistics NV · corporate · customer since 2016
cases.brief: A long-standing customer changes its ownership structure. Screening returns no hits.
cases.opening: Nothing has fired. The relationship manager flagged this himself: the customer restructured its shareholding three months ago and the new holders sit conspicuously below every threshold that would have triggered anything.

actions.name: Screen every entity in the chain, not just the customer
Review transaction flows since the restructure

e_struct.title: Ownership map
e_struct.body: Three new corporate shareholders replaced the previous single holder: Baltic Freight OÜ (24%), Anchor Marine Ltd (23%), Verda Holdings Sàrl (22%). Remaining 31% held by the original founder. No single holder above 25%.

e_aggregate.title: Aggregated ownership
e_aggregate.body: Baltic Freight OÜ and Anchor Marine Ltd are both ultimately majority-owned by the same designated individual. Combined: 47%. Under the 50% rule the designated person does not control Northwind — but combined with Verda, in which he holds a 40% stake, indirect economic interest reaches 55.8%.

e_sanc.title: Chain-wide screening
e_sanc.body: Screening the customer returns nothing. Screening every entity in the chain returns a designated individual two levels up, listed under EU Regulation 269/2014 since 2022. He appears nowhere on the customer's own record.

e_control.title: Control rights
e_control.body: The shareholders' agreement grants Baltic and Anchor jointly the right to appoint three of five board members and a veto over asset disposals. Control exists independently of the percentages.

e_tx.title: Flows since the restructure
e_tx.body: Freight receipts unchanged in pattern. One new payment corridor to a jurisdiction the customer has not previously traded with, €340,000 across four payments.

e_media.title: Adverse media
e_media.body: Two trade-press articles on the restructure, describing it as a management buy-in. No mention of the ultimate holder.

e_rm.title: Relationship manager
e_rm.body: "They told me it was a succession plan. I thought it was odd that three buyers appeared at once, which is why I raised it. That's as far as my knowledge goes."

e_legal.title: Restructuring documents
e_legal.body: Share purchase agreements executed on the same day, before the same notary, with sequential document numbers. The three transactions were not independent.

close.title: Closed a sanctions-evasion structure
close.body: The screening returned nothing because the designated person was never on the customer's record. The structure was built precisely to produce that result, and it worked.

rfi.title: Asked the customer about its own ownership
rfi.body: The structure was designed to be asked about. You will receive a coherent, documented answer that confirms the surface facts you already have.

escalate.title: Escalated the structure
escalate.body: Right that this needed to leave your desk. But a sanctions nexus is not an ordinary escalation — asset-freeze obligations bite immediately, and the timing of the report matters.

sar.title: Reported, with the aggregation set out
sar.body: You identified what the screening could not: that no single holding breaches a threshold, that the aggregate does, and that control sits with parties connected to a designated individual. This is the case sanctions screening is structurally unable to find on its own.

cases.epilogue_wrong: Fourteen months later the structure surfaces in an EU enforcement action. The institution's exposure is characterised as a failure to look through a chain that was, on the record, visible from the documents it already held.
cases.law: EU Regulation 269/2014 — asset freezes extend to entities owned or controlled by designated persons; AMLR Art. 22 — beneficial ownership; Art. 34 — EDD.
cases.lesson: Sanctions screening matches names on the record in front of it. A structure built two levels up will never appear there. The 50% rule aggregates across chains and the control limb applies regardless of percentage — which means the only reliable defence is looking through the chain, and almost nobody does it unprompted.
